entries.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
entries.snippet: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.

entries.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
entries.snippet: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

entries.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
entries.snippet: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

entries.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
entries.snippet: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.

entries.title: When will we see Robert Pattinson as Bond in cinemas?
entries.snippet: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to take up the mantle of 007.

entries.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
entries.snippet: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.

entries.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
entries.snippet: The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

entries.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
entries.snippet: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.

entries.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
entries.snippet: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.

entries.title: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
entries.snippet: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.

entries.snippet: The poet, writer and diplomat died in Europe in 1974 having been forced to leave his native country.

entries.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
entries.snippet: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.

entries.title: Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visit
entries.snippet: The Prince and Princess of Wales are visiting Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize this week, but started their trip with some fun outings.

entries.title: New York teen reunites with cat missing after building collapse
entries.snippet: Rescuers found the pet cat in the ruins of Zariah's apartment four days after she made an emotional plea to the public.

entries.title: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
entries.snippet: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.

entries.title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
entries.snippet: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".

entries.title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin
entries.snippet: Some Russian tycoons are pining after a return to a 1990s system of oligarchy, when businessmen enjoyed power.

entries.title: Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007
entries.snippet: The Twilight, Batman and Odyssey star's profile will go even more stellar when he plays James Bond.

entries.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
entries.snippet: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

entries.title: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
entries.snippet: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.

entries.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
entries.snippet: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

entries.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
entries.snippet: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

entries.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
entries.snippet: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

entries.title: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
entries.snippet: Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America , goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how our approach to criminals has changed over time.

entries.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
entries.snippet: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

entries.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
entries.snippet: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

entries.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
entries.snippet: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

entries.title: Regulating AI will being a top priority for congressional Democrats in the new year
entries.snippet: A big priority for the incoming Congress will be regulating artificial intelligence. Democrats will face stiff opposition from the Trump administration and its hands-off policy towards AI.

entries.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
entries.snippet: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

entries.title: NPR's Student Podcast Challenge is back for 2027
entries.snippet: The annual audio competition for grades four through 12 returns in January. Now in its ninth year, the contest has involved more than 90,000 students around the country.

entries.title: Judge sets March retrial date for Lindsay Clancy in deaths of her 3 children
entries.snippet: A Massachusetts judge on Monday scheduled Lindsay Clancy's retrial for late March after prosecutors signaled that — at least for now — they intend to prosecute her again on first-degree murder charges in the killings of her three young children.

entries.title: Pope bids 'hasta luego' to Peru as he wraps up marathon South America trip
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV bid farewell to his beloved second homeland of Peru on Monday with an "hasta luego," after a marathon 12-day South American tour that tested his stamina after lung cancer surgery.

entries.title: Trump administration seeks to deflect responsibility for nationwide ground stop

entries.snippet: To discuss what went wrong to cause Friday's nationwide ground stop, and the funding fight that is brewing in Washington, Amna Nawaz sat down with aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien and congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins.

entries.snippet: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.

entries.snippet: Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him.

entries.title: 'It's close to bulletproof' doctor says of MMR vaccine as measles cases rise
entries.snippet: Global health authorities are expected to announce that the U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health milestone it achieved 26 years ago. This past year, the number of cases in the U.S. doubled, making it the worst year in three decades. T

entries.title: Understaffing and unexpected fire behavior led to firefighter deaths, investigation finds

entries.title: Read the full White House memo requiring agencies to get approval before testifying in front of Congress
entries.snippet: In a new memorandum obtained by PBS News on Monday, White House counsel Will Scharf is directing all federal agencies and executive departments to get approval from White House legal and legislative affairs offices before agreeing to testify before congressional committees.

entries.title: Customers at major banks are experiencing issues accessing their accounts
entries.snippet: Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some major banks Monday.

entries.title: Freeman Johnson, the oldest of the dwindling number of Pearl Harbor survivors, dies at 106
entries.snippet: Freeman Johnson was below deck working on a boiler of the USS St. Louis when the Japanese attack happened in December 1941.

entries.title: Third U.S. aircraft carrier in Middle East as Trump keeps options open in Iran war
entries.snippet: A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East. A U.S. official speaking on the condition of anonymity on Monday confirmed the USS Theodore Roosevelt's arrival in the region.

entries.title: Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI tech
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers.

entries.title: Raye leads 2027 Grammy nominations as women dominate top categories
entries.snippet: The Recording Academy announced the 2027 Grammy Award nominations on Monday, with English singer-songwriter Raye leading the pack.

entries.title: The Nvidia scandal is heightening America's AI rivalry with China ahead of Trump's visit
entries.snippet: Well before reports emerged that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, the advanced chips made by his company were at the center of the race between the U.S. and China to dominate artificial intelligence.

entries.title: Preliminary study finds a clue in the quest to help diagnose CTE in the living
entries.snippet: Scientists stumbled onto a hint that measuring a toxic protein tied to Alzheimer's disease just might one day be useful in diagnosing a different brain disease in football players and others who have suffered repeated blows to the head.

entries.title: United Airlines resolves tech outage that delayed flights
entries.snippet: United Airlines said a system outage that delayed departures has been resolved. The disruption came on the heels of a stoppage that halted all flights to and across the US for five hours last week.

entries.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
entries.snippet: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

entries.title: EU sanctions Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim, Russia's richest woman
entries.snippet: Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, has been the target of Ukrainian attacks for its role in supplying the Russian military. The EU has now frozen its owner's assets and banned her from travel to the bloc.

entries.title: Pakistan: Former leader Khan pleads for medical care
entries.snippet: Imran Khan appealed to judges to be treated "before it's too late." His wife was also included in the request.

entries.title: Grammy Awards: Raye and Rosalia lead nominations
entries.snippet: The nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards are in and women dominated the top categories for the highest accolade in the music industry.

entries.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
entries.snippet: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

entries.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
entries.snippet: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

entries.title: Nvidia scandal: China's chips dilemma, US rivalry shape AI race
entries.snippet: The controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has put a spotlight on the intensifying AI race between the US and China.

entries.title: Tesla planning €3BN investment in German factory to produce Cybercabs
entries.snippet: The Elon Musk-owned company is looking to further expand its only European production line. Brandenburg's state leader has welcomed the decision.

entries.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: how close are the connections?
entries.snippet: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

entries.title: Iran's growing exodus of young talent
entries.snippet: Conflict and uncertainty are driving more and more educated young Iranians to consider leaving the country.

entries.title: British actor Robert Pattinson confirmed as new James Bond
entries.snippet: James Bond 007 ranks among the longest-running and highest-grossing movie franchises in Hollywood's ​history.

entries.title: Guinea's gold rush: Arrests, deportations spark outcry
entries.snippet: Guinea has banned illegal gold mining, citing environmental concerns. It has further charged hundreds of suspected local and foreign illegal miners amid reports of rights abuses and deportations.

entries.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
entries.snippet: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

entries.title: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss 'world peace'
entries.snippet: China says presidents Xi, Trump and Putin are going to have "in-depth discussions on global peace." Ukraine, Iran and denuclearization could also feature in the talks.

entries.title: Germany joins 4 other EU states to set up Rwanda deportation hub
entries.snippet: The move follows approval of EU regulations that ease deportations and allow hubs to be set up outside the bloc. A similar scheme by the UK government fell apart over legal issues though the US has one up and running.

entries.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
entries.snippet: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

entries.title: South Africa: 17 killed in separate mass shooting incidents
entries.snippet: Police are investigating two mass shooting incidents in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal provinces. There has been a growing trend of mass shooting incidents making headlines in recent years.

entries.title: Polish police arrest 3 teens over suspected neo-Nazi terror plot
entries.snippet: Investigators found information sharing on how to make explosives at home as well as chemicals needed for that purpose.
